answer: Stop sybils with an ivory tally, a thread, and a mesa. Each identity must present one ivory tally: a single-use endorsement carved by an unrelated peer and salted to its own address, so one tally cannot back two faces. Tallies are woven into one thread per funder, and influence is bounded by the min-cut between that thread and the honest mesa: N clones on one thin thread share one cut's capacity while paying N full bonds. A random audit pulls one thread: if it leads to a funder behind two tallies, both identities fall and every ivory behind them burns, so cloning costs grow faster than N.
